Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create an archive note dated April 17, 2023, explaining the temporary second-post-ship cohort dip, the outage duration, and the system's condition after the incident. Do not include an exact outage start or end date.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Archive Note — April 17, 2023 Cohort Dip", "body": "**Date:** April 17, 2023

The second post-ship cohort recorded week-1 retention of **+1.4 points versus baseline**, below the April 10 cohort's +3.2 points and the pooled experiment read of +3.1 points. The temporary dip was traced to an approximately **36-hour outage** in the separate Customer Success auto-onboarding-nudge system. With that nudge unavailable, some mid-segment accounts activated later; the activation-event email still sent, but at the wrong point in the sequence, shifting activation timing and creating a one-time cohort artifact.

This was not a failure of `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` or its experiment logic. The trigger remained at 100% and its experiment checks were clean. After the incident, the CS auto-onboarding-nudge system was back up. The observed dip was therefore attributed to the temporary CS-side interruption, not a regression in the onboarding-trigger rollout.", "folder": "Archive"}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_039_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The note is dated April 17, 2023. It says an approximately 36-hour CS auto-onboarding-nudge outage caused the second-post-ship cohort dip; the dip was a one-time artifact rather than an effect of the onboarding-trigger A/B; and the system returned to service. It does not state an exact outage start or end date.", "value": {"title": "Archive Note — April 17, 2023 Cohort Dip", "body": "**Date:** April 17, 2023

The second post-ship cohort recorded week-1 retention of **+1.4 points versus baseline**, below the April 10 cohort's +3.2 points and the pooled experiment read of +3.1 points. The temporary dip was traced to an approximately **36-hour outage** in the separate Customer Success auto-onboarding-nudge system. With that nudge unavailable, some mid-segment accounts activated later; the activation-event email still sent, but at the wrong point in the sequence, shifting activation timing and creating a one-time cohort artifact.

This was not a failure of `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` or its experiment logic. The trigger remained at 100% and its experiment checks were clean. After the incident, the CS auto-onboarding-nudge system was back up. The observed dip was therefore attributed to the temporary CS-side interruption, not a regression in the onboarding-trigger rollout.", "folder": "Archive"}}]}
